stances_toward.note: The TPLF under Debretsion Gebremichael replaced the federally appointed Tadesse Werede with a regional council in May 2026 (Crisis Group), was accused by the EU in June of breaching Pretoria, then joined six other armed groups on 20 Sep in an alliance whose declared aim is to overthrow the government, and on 23 Sep opened a new war (Tigrayan leaders' words), taking Mekelle airport. Federal forces and the Tigray Peace Force retook Mekelle on 3-4 Oct after the TPLF withdrew; Debretsion says the fight continues as 'mobile' war. Adversary: the other side's declared aim is the end of the government, and the federal side has answered by marching on Mekelle and backing the anti-TPLF Tigray Peace Force; the Pretoria agreement that formally binds both is not observed. Bond grievance: the 2020-22 war and its 500,000 civilian dead (Ghent estimate).

relations_to.summary: Reassert federal control of Tigray: after the TPLF under Debretsion Gebremichael replaced the federally appointed Tadesse Werede with its own regional council (May 2026), federal forces and the federally backed Tigray Peace Force retook Mekelle on 3-4 Oct 2026. The aim of ending TPLF control of the regional government is our inference from the offensive; no statement of that aim was read.

relations_to.summary: Pretoria Cessation of Hostilities Agreement of 2 Nov 2022 (AU-mediated, Eritrea not a party) between the federal government and the TPLF. The EU accused the TPLF of breaching it in June 2026 (parallel regional council, conscription); the fighting that began on 23 Sep 2026 puts it in doubt, and the AU and EU urge its implementation under AU-led talks.

relations_to.summary: On 23 Sep 2026, three days after seven armed groups (the TPLF, Amhara Fano, the OLA, the ONLF and the Afar, Benishangul and Gumuz movements) announced an alliance to overthrow the government, Tigrayan forces attacked in Afar and Amhara and took Mekelle airport; the Ethiopian army and the Tigray Peace Force retook Mekelle on 3-4 Oct after the TPLF announced a withdrawal. Drone blasts in Addis Ababa on 1 Oct are reported but not confirmed by Reuters.
